name: Emil Wiechert
summary: German physicist and geophysicist, director of the first Institute of Geophysics in Göttingen and inventor of the Wiechert seismograph.

name: Tilsit
summary: Town in the Province of Prussia, now Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia.

name: Albertus University in Königsberg
summary: University in Königsberg where Wiechert studied sciences and physics.

name: University of Göttingen
summary: University in Göttingen where Wiechert worked and established the Institute of Geophysics.

name: Institut für Geophysik
summary: First Institute of Geophysics in the world, founded in Göttingen by Wiechert.

name: Erdbebenhaus
summary: Building constructed in 1902 in the garden of the Institute of Geophysics to house seismographs.

name: Wiechert seismograph
summary: Sensitive mechanical seismometers with air-damped pendulums invented by Wiechert.

name: Ludger Mintrop
summary: Student of Wiechert who conducted seismic exploration experiments with a steel ball.

name: Mintrop-Kugel
summary: 4 ton steel ball used by Mintrop to generate man-made earthquakes for seismic exploration.

name: German Geophysical Society
summary: Scientific society founded in 1922 on the initiative of Wiechert.

name: Gustav Angenheister Sen.
summary: Director of the institute and observatory after Wiechert's death until after World War II.

name: Manfred Siebert
summary: Director of the institute from 1964 to 1992 who played an important role in saving the observatory.

name: Wolfgang Brunk
summary: Chairman of the working group Technology of Measurement Valley and founding chairman of the society.

name: Wiechert'sche Erdbebenwarte Göttingen e.V.
summary: Registered society founded in 2005 to own and operate the observatory.

name: Göttingen
summary: City in Germany where the Institute of Geophysics and observatory are located.
